item.title: Ride for ruin with our Rohan™ tactical advice
item.description: Top tactical tips from a Middle-earth™ Strategy Battle Game veteran.
item.content:encoded:
With the updated Riders of Rohan thundering across the battlefields of Middle-earth, we decided it was time to get some tactical tips for all Marshals of the Riddermark. Fortunately for us, Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game community veteran Kalman Steels answered our call for aid in a thorough assessment of the armies of Rohan.

Kalman: The Kingdom of Rohan really doesn’t need much of an introduction. A favourite for movie and book fans alike, it is also one of the most popular factions in the Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game. Famous for their glorious and devastating cavalry charges, Rohan are the faction to use if you want to ride out and meet your opponent for death and glory.* 

I’ll begin by looking at the strengths and weaknesses that come with a Rohan army, and then dig into how to make the most of them on the battlefield. 

Strengths

A host of different lists to choose from

The Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game is broken down into Army Lists. Each one represents a faction with their own special rules from a certain point in Middle-earth’s history. Rohan has 10 Army Lists to choose from, such as Riders of Théoden, Army of Edoras, or the Fords of Isen, but Rohan models can also be taken in four other lists with other factions, such as Men of the West and The Grief of Éomer. Having the choice of 14 lists means you can have a Rohan force ready for any Scenario.

A wide and varied choice of Heroes

Rohan has some of the most famous and recognisable Heroes from The Lord of the RingsTM movies and novels, with the likes of Théoden, Éomer, Éowyn, Helm Hammerhand, and Héra. With each Hero adding something different to your army, you can adapt your force to counter any foe.

Excellent Cavalry

It goes without saying that Rohan are the horse lords – they even have a special rule with that very name, amongst a few others. Riders of Rohan can gallop effortlessly over the battlefield with their 10" move, getting into the perfect position to strike on their terms. Due to the Cavalry Charge rule and the bonuses it provides, when the forces of Rohan choose to engage, they can sweep their foes from the field.

Bows

Every Rider of Rohan comes with a bow. Every single one. Riders of Rohan can unleash deadly volleys of arrows to thin out their opponent’s ranks before lining up a glorious cavalry charge to win the day. A common tactic for Rohan players is to ‘kite and shoot’ their opponent until the time is right – at first light on the fifth day.

Weaknesses

Low model count when using only Cavalry

Taking an all-Cavalry list can quickly erode the points you have to spend on your army. After taking your favourite Heroes, you may not have a lot of space for a suitable model count. Experienced Rohan players will try to find that perfect balance between having all the cool stuff and including enough models. The last thing you want is to Charge in and then quickly be mobbed by hordes of Orcs!

Fortunately, Heroes like Éomer and Helm Hammerhand can easily make up for their army’s lower model count, each capable of carving a swathe through their foes.

Low Defence

Riders and Warriors of Rohan don’t tend to wear a lot of heavy armour, relying instead on keeping the foe at a distance until the time is right. As the majority of the army has a humble Defence 5, Rohan armies can’t take as many hits as others, or risk being exposed to enemy shooting for too long. Use the speed of your Cavalry to close in quickly with the foe, or ensure that there is plenty of intervening terrain between your warriors and enemy missile weapons.

Getting bogged down

Rohan armies, especially all-Cavalry armies, will often find themselves outnumbered on the battlefield. With Rohan’s strength being in the cavalry charge, losing Priority roll-offs and getting counter-charged by hordes of infantry can spell doom for a force of Rohirrim. Holding some of your Cavalry back in a flying reserve will give you a second wave of charging riders that can help toImitigate losing a key Priority roll-off.

Too much choice

Whilst this is a nicer problem to have, Rohan players have lots of awesome Heroes to choose from. In total, Rohan has 21 Hero profiles from both the Armies of the Lord of the RingsTM and the Armies of Middle-earthTM supplements. Mustering a Rohan army will leave you spoilt for choice! But I’ll give you some advice… Éomer, choose Éomer!** You’re then allowed to shout “To the King!” every time you move him.

Strategy

Using Cavalry

As we now know, if you choose to muster a Rohan force centred around Cavalry, you will often find yourself outnumbered, but there are tactics to help you achieve victory even against the vast legions of the enemy.

When starting the game, you ideally want to identify areas on the board you can use to effectively ‘kite and shoot’ your opponent with your bows. For the first few turns of the game, you want to try to bring your opponent’s model count down, and if possible, draw them into a better position for when you eventually Charge – for example, encircling them or leading them away from vital objectives that your fast-moving Cavalry can easily return to as the battle progresses.

Models armed with bows can move up to half their Move Value and still Shoot. This means that your Riders of Rohan can Move up to 5" (almost the full Move of an average Infantry model) and still loose their arrows. When this tactic is used correctly, your Riders will always just be out of reach – but can always forgo a turn of Shooting in order to leave the enemy behind if they need to. This is a strong tactic as it gives your opponent one of two choices: run at you and risk breaking up their formation, or stand still whilst being pelted by arrows. 

Choosing the right list for your playstyle

As noted above, Rohan players have a wide choice of Army Lists to muster from. Each one of these lists has different special rules to represent a particular scene from the films or books. Some lists are Cavalry-heavy, whereas others are mainly made up of Warriors of Rohan, such as Defenders of Helm’s Deep. When choosing and subsequently playing a certain list, you want to make sure you maximise these special rules to your advantage.

For example, if your playstyle is to lean into the ‘kite and shoot’ mechanic of the army, you wouldn’t choose the list ‘Ride Out’, as it features a special rule called Now for wrath, now for ruin, and the red dawn, which means that all your Cavalry models must Charge if able. On the flip side, if you want an army that crushes the foe as it sallies forth, then Ride Out may be for you, as that same special rule makes your Cavalry even better on the Charge!

If you’re looking to field more Infantry than Cavalry, then I recommend Defenders of the Hornburg, as this list has Héra, the Bride of Death and the furious Helm, Wraith of the Hornburg leading Warriors of Rohan. I’ve played this list a lot over the past year, and have found Helm to be one of the most enjoyable Heroes in the game as he goes around punching foes with his bare ‘hammerhands’.

Finally, if you’re looking for a more balanced Rohan Army, Riders of Théoden and Riders of Éomer will be right up your street. The Riders of Théoden Army has a special rule to represent the greatest cavalry charge in cinematic history, while the Riders of Éomer can bring Gandalf the White to battle, who can utilise the light of the dawn to blind your enemy as you close with them

Heroes

The biggest challenge you will have is choosing which of your favourite characters to take. However in certain lists, some Heroes are crucial.

In the Riders of Éomer list, the Marshal of the Riddermark becomes unleashed. He gains the special rule “To the King”, allowing him to call a free Heroic Combat once per turn. A Heroic Combat allows you to Move and Fight again if you slay all the models you began the phase in Combat with. Combining this with the Cavalry Charge bonuses turns Éomer into a meatgrinder who can happily slay four or five enemies a turn. His horse, Firefoot, also has a whopping 12" Move, just to make sure no one escapes his wrath.

Another unique Hero is Lief, Page of Helm. Lief is not a melee beast like Éomer. He will often find himself sitting behind the battle lines handing out the Orders from Edoras, buffing your Army when needed. Lief can issue up to five orders per game and each order, when used at the right time, can spell doom for your opponent. For example, he can make all Rohan Hero models within 3" declare a Heroic Combat for free, which can be devastating. He can also allow your models to Move further or Shoot more accurately. All of this makes him a great, versatile and cost-effective Hero option.

Finally, we have the humble Captain of Rohan. As Rohan has so many named Heroes to choose from, Captains are often overlooked, but they can be great additions to your army.

There are two main reasons for this. The first is their points cost – as a cheap option they allow you to fit more models in your army compared to taking an expensive named Hero. Secondly, every Captain is able to call a Heroic March. When they do this, they can make Infantry models move an additional 3" and Cavalry move an additional 5". The only caveat is that you are not allowed to Charge if you take part in a Heroic March. Nevertheless, if you want to get into a better position quicker, or beat your opponent to an objective, Heroic March speeds you on your way.

Final Thoughts

The Kingdom of Rohan is a fantastic faction for both veterans and beginners alike. They have access to so many different Army Lists and Heroes that once you have an army fully mustered, you’ll be able to try out different rules, tactics and playstyles for ages to come. Before long you will be fearing no darkness and shouting “Forth Eorlingas!”.

* Yes, Kalman has tried to squeeze in as many lines from the films as he possibly can.
** We think the Third Marshal of the Riddermark might be Kalman’s favourite.

item.title: Warhammer Age of Sigmar – Quarterly Battlescroll Updates
item.description: See the latest rules updates from the Mortal Realms.
item.content:encoded:
We’re a few months into the season of Warhammer Age of Sigmar, so it’s time for the first of the quarterly Battlescroll updates. 

Points adjustments are complemented by some important rules changes to improve balance in the Mortal Realms and below you can find a summary of the most significant updates.

Universal

There are a couple of changes that open up list building options. Firstly, a number of infantry heroes can now be included in regiments, and a lot of units have had their reinforcement restrictions lifted. 

Grand Alliance Order

A couple of rules from the Scourge of Aqshy season rules have proven to be more powerful than anticipated and so are being toned down a little. Fyreslayers can no longer use Blazing Impetus to move after being set up, and for the Idoneth Deepkin, Abyssal Dweller no longer reduces enemy movement. The War Hydra from the Cities of Sigmar battletome supplement has also had its Impossible to Destroy ability tweaked as it was proving, well, impossible to destroy.

Grand Alliance Chaos

On the Skaven side, Krittok Foulblade can now use his A Reputation for Cunning ability without needing to spend a Command Point, and the Lightning Master ability of the Warlock Galvaneer is now guaranteed to activate, yes-yes! For the Slaves to Darkness the Oracular Visions of the Sorcerer Lord are now more reliable, but units with an Ensorcelled Banner can no longer switch Pledge to Chaos keywords. You chose your Dark God and now you’re stuck with them!

The newest addition to Grand Alliance Chaos – the Helsmiths of Hashut – have had their battle formations updated. The studio felt they were not having the impact hoped for and so the Zharrdron now have some new tools as they seek to claim dominion over the Mortal Realms.

Grand Alliance Death

The Nighthaunt have had the most changes in this quarter’s update with improvements to the Lord Vitriolic and Scriptor Mortis, while the Shadowy Aura heroic trait now blocks visibility to Nighthaunt infantry and cavalry, and there’s been a boost to the Death Stalkers battle formation. The Ossiarch Bonereapers no longer have to pay the Relentless Discipline ‘tax’ for reinforced units, so abilities such as Pitiless Assault just got cheaper for your larger units.

The Scourge of Aqshy Vengorian Lord has been proving slightly too powerful so the Soulblight Gravelords Monster Frenzied Surge ability has been adjusted.

Grand Alliance Destruction

Finally, the Gatebreaker Mega-Gargant from the Scourge of Aqshy has undergone a little change so that he doesn’t form an over-the-top combo with the new Rock-hurlers.

item.title: See Warhammer Tone Pro paints in action on Warhammer TV
item.description: Plus, Combat Patrol battles and Ork lore added this week.
item.content:encoded:
Ultimate Paint Off gets to grips with the Warhammer Tone Pro paint range on Warhammer TV this week.

On top of that, fighting starts in the new Tale of Four Gamers campaign series as the hobbyists launch their first Combat Patrol games, and you can learn more about Ork clans on Loremasters.

Available on Thursday: Ultimate Paint Off – Limited Palette

In the first of a three-part series showing off the Warhammer Tone Pro range for the first time, Ultimate Paint Off challenges the contestants to paint a miniature with just three colour groups – that’s a measly 15 pots of paint.

What we know that the contestants don’t when they choose their paints is that they’ll be painting a Space Marine, and they’ll have to include a freehand element and a unique Chapter symbol. See what these fantastic painters are able to do with a limited number of colours. 

Available tomorrow: Tale of Four Gamers – Warhammer 40,000

Earlier this month we met the four players taking part in our ongoing Tale of Four Gamers campaign, and today their first few units threw down in the Combat Patrol arena. They’ll be discussing what went right, what went wrong, and how they’ll be expanding their armies from here, as the drums of war are only beginning to rumble and there’ll be plenty more battles to come. 

Stay tuned over the next few months as we check in on their painting progress, throw them into perilous missions, and ultimately crown a champion.

Available now: Loremasters – Ork Clans

The major Clans that form the bedrock of Ork society have a monumental impact on how the average Boy thinks and fights, and today Loremasters presenter Alex sneaks alarmingly close to find out exactly what separates a Goff or a Bad Moon from a Snakebite or a Blood Axe. The concept of unity in an Ork horde might sound laughable, but the Clan structure is the closest thing they have to family ties, and it pays to know just how much you can tell from an Ork by the Clan they associate with.

Available on Friday: Adepta Sororitas: Penitence

Enjoy the action-packed animated series Adepta Sororitas: Penitence in a single show with the final cut version which brings together all three parts. Can a squad of Battle Sisters deliver a holy relic after their shuttle is shot down by brutal Ork Kommandos?

You’ll also be able to enjoy the original score – ideal for putting on while you’re painting.

Introducing Warhammer Tone Pro – 30 new colours, in 5 tones for a total of 150 new Warhammer paints. 

Warhammer Tone Pro brings amazing colour intensity and coverage, with great flow characteristics that will help you achieve your best results.

Five tones, infinite possibilities

The new Tone Pro paint range is made up of 30 different colours, each with 5 tones. The tones are numbered, with 1 the darkest and 5 the lightest – making it simple to identify highlights and shades for your chosen colours, and build up layers.

Incredible Coverage

Warhammer Tone Pro gives superb coverage from the first application. This isn’t just for your blues and dark greens, but even yellow and white – making for faster, bolder painting.

Intense Colour

These colours are vivid. Vibrant pigmentation means brilliant whites, electrifying yellows, scintillating magentas, intense reds… and the rest.

One paint for any technique

Tone Pro’s new formulation enables it to be used for any technique – applying basecoats or layers, picking out highlights, glazing, or drybrushing. What’s more, you can mix any Tone Pro paint with the Shading Medium to turn it into a shade or glaze. There’s also a Blending Medium that extends the drying time of your paint, giving you more time to blend your colours together.

There are also four new dry brushes – sized from XS to L – that pair with the new paints to make it even easier to get a smoother finish without the chalky effect that drybrushing can sometimes give.

item.title: The Big Autumn Preview – The Legion of the Damned enter the killzone
item.description: Spectral Space Marines battle Ork Nobz in a new Kill Team box.
item.content:encoded:
After years as little more than whispered legends, the Legion of the Damned return to the 41st Millennium in a new Kill Team box set amidst the unending slaughter on Armageddon.

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

The Legion of the Damned step forth from a halo of witchfire to unleash burning retribution on the xenos brutes. With fire and fury, they take on the elite Ork Nobz Mob and bring aid to the beleaguered planet. 

Each spectral Legionnaire is covered in skeletal details and wreathed in ethereal flames. Their true nature eludes even the most persistent of Inquisitors, and though they can be credited with turning the tide of countless battles, few know to whom – or what – they owe their lives.

The Legion’s mysterious, ghostly nature makes this kill team play wildly differently from other Space Marines, as they must solidify their connection to the material plane over time to reach the height of their power. Early in the game, they move and fight slower than regular Space Marines, but as turning points tick over and their form solidifies, they grow to become terrifying, spectral monsters, bursting at the seams with eldritch fire.

Against them stands a team of vicious Boss Nobz – the cream of the Orks’ elite warriors. You may have seen them in our reveal, or inside Codex: Orks, but the Kill Team:Armageddon boxed set is where they will be available first.

These hardcore veterans have survived wars on dozens of worlds and tower over their lesser kin, adorned in thick armour plates and carrying a wide variety of eclectic Ork weapons. Some are obsessed with dakka and dual-wield kustom shootas, while others delight in flame-fuelled destruction and heft an enormous skorcha* into the killzone.

Speaking of killzones, a whole new set of terrain is the battleground for this clash of fire and fury, with wrecked vehicles and crumbling buildings painting a picture of the devastation unleashed upon Armageddon.

The Killzone: Armageddon terrain is designed to stylistically fit in with the existing Battlezone Fronteris kits, but in a more battle-worn state. You get two sturdy bunkers, which have their own rules for the desperate close-quarters fights that happen when an unlucky operative has to storm one. There are also ruins and scatter terrain, including a wrecked Redemptor Dreadnought and Rogal Dorn Battle Tank.

To top it all off, you get the customary sets of datacards to help keep your important rules in mind, and the Kill Team: Armageddon Dossier, which contains all of the rules you need for both kill teams as well as background lore on the Legion of the Damned, Ork Nobz, and the desperate times that threw these bitter foes together.

We can’t wait to see the Legion of the Damned back on the tabletop, and we’ll be taking a closer look at their rules (for both Kill Team AND Warhammer 40,000) as we get closer to release. While we wait for them to rematerialise, check out the other big reveals from the Big Autumn Preview.

item.title: The Big Autumn Preview – A new duardin faction revealed!
item.description: Witness the might of the Khazalite Holds as they sally forth from the mountains.
item.content:encoded:
The ironclad gates have opened, and the Khazalite Holds are on the warpath. Meet the new Warhammer Age of Sigmar faction!

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

The Khazalites consider themselves the truest and most respectable of all duardin, as it is they who venerate the Ancestor Gods with due reverence, and they who maintain the honourable traditions of their forebears. It is not with mercantile pragmatism or mercenary fury that the realms will be cleansed of the hated Skaven, but with stony resilience and relentless determination.

The Khazalite Holds are preparing to march on the Mortal Realms with a new Army Set – packed with miniatures and a battletome – and followed by a range of other new kits.

Led by the mighty Hjulda Drakkblud, this force of indomitable warriors has everything the Khazalites do best: tough armour, deadly hammers, and a cannon big enough to blow a hole through a Mega-Gargant. It’s a complete Spearhead army in a box, and also serves as the perfect starting point for a wider Khazalite Holds collection.

Hjulda herself is legendary among those Khazalites who have rejoined the surface world, as she and her Clanguard search endlessly for lost karaks that might yet be reclaimed, hopeful that the next might finally be the home of her lost clan.

Accompanying her are 10 Clanshields – doughty warriors armed with a variety of Kromdron weapons – which can be axes, hammers, or a mix – that specialise in taking out enemy infantry. Clad in stout armour, they are difficult to shift, and they invoke the names and deeds of their ancestors to bring them strength in battle.

Of particular note are the massive Gholems of Gazul – animated stone constructs that honour the Ancestor God of the underworlds. They stand sentinel inside duardin tombs until called upon by a mournful dirge of remembrance, silently trudging into battle with stoic purpose as they send scores of foes to the Realm of Death with great swings of their stone hammers.

Supplying the duardin with long-ranged firepower is the Oathkeeper Cannon. Combining engineering excellence with esoteric runecraft, these war machines tear through enemy ranks with ease. As the firing rune is struck, it’s almost as if Grungni himself has smashed the foes of the duardin with his mighty forging hammer.

The army set also includes the new battletome, packed with background lore on this new faction and the rules you need to unleash them in battle. It has a special cover, which you’ll only find in the army set, and there are also 53 warscroll cards.

Battletome: Khazalite Holds

The battletome will also be coming out separately at a later date, packed with the same in-depth lore and inspiring artwork. It’s not just the newcomers who occupy the battletome’s pages either, as the Fyreslayers will be joining their duardin cousins (more on them lower down this article!).

Beyond the Army Set, a second wave of Khazalite Holds units expand the army even further, starting with the Thrynns and Runewrights that lead them.

Thrynn and Runewright

Thrynns are the lords of the Karaks, chosen by their fellow nobles. Armed and armoured with the finest runic artefacts, they lead the war throngs into battle. Runewrights are masters of arcane forging, able to utilise the resonant magic of the runes.

High Kyng Valankrom

Above them all stands High Kyng Valankrom, the supreme leader of the Khazalite Holds, crowned by Grungni himself. He is a ferocious warrior and shrewd statesman, unquestioned in his authority, and he rides into battle on an immense stone construct known as a War Throne. The War Throne moves across the earth, impelled by powerful duardin magic.

This jaw-dropping centrepiece kit also builds a Thrynn on War Throne. It is a great honour to ride such a war altar into battle, and it inspires nearby Khazalite Holds troops to ever greater feats.

Clangunners

The Clanshields from the army set aren’t the only new infantry – they’re joined by the Clangunners. Picking off enemies at range with accurate thrundok rifles or devastating them closer up with thrundrin shotcannons, they excel in both defence and attack.

Stonebreaker Mortar

The Oathkeeper Cannon from the army box can alternatively be built as a Stonebreaker Mortar. This devastating war machine specialises in destroying enemy infantry and, when the correct rune is struck, can even devastate more than one target with its blast.

Valayan Guardians

Among the finest troops available to a Khazalite Hold, Valayan Guardians fight for the very heart of duardin society and place the defence of their kin as the highest honour. Valaya is the ancestor of hearth and home – known as the defender – and the Guardians believe that she watches over their every battle, which inspires them to fight with incredible tenacity and resilience (even for a duardin!)

Gholems of Valaya

Speaking of Valaya, the Gholems of Gazul also have an alternate build option, making them Gholems of Valaya instead. Carved into the image of the warrior goddess, they are treated with utmost reverence by her followers.

Fyreslayers

As mentioned above, the Fyreslayers – or Grimmdron – have become part of the Khazalite Holds. After decades of slow attrition grinding down their magmaholds, and a disastrous attack on their spiritual capital by a tenuous alliance of Helsmiths and Skaven, the slayers of Grimnir are filled with a burning need for vengeance.

This means that you’ll be able to use your existing miniatures with the new battletome, whether you want to run a full Fyreslayers army, or want to include some alongside the new Kromdron. We’ll be talking more about how this affects them as we get closer to release.

Ormyr and Ashtongue

The Fyreslayers are getting a new wandering beastmaster, Ormyr, for their war party, who comes accompanied by his kyndledroth Ashtongue. This eclectic pair are known across the realms of the Khazalites, notorious for turning up out of nowhere to offer their aid on the eve of battle.

Regiment of Renown

Troubled by the fall of the Fyreslayer kingdom, Fjori and his like-minded Grimmdron sell their services to the highest bidder – as long as they can also slake their desire for vengeance. This new Regiment of Renown can be used by any Order army, and includes an Auric Flamekeeper, a Grimhold Exile, and five Hearthguard Berzerkers.

Spearhead: Magmic Fyrd

Burning with vengeance for the destruction of their former holds and lands, the Magmic Fyrds of the Grimmdron seek out foes wherever they can find them. This Fyreslayer-themed Spearhead features a monstrous Magmadroth ridden by a Runefather, a Runesmiter, nine Vulkyn Flameseekers, and five Auric Hearthguard.

That’s a lot to see from a brand new faction, isn’t it? We’ll have loads more details for you as we get closer to pre-order day, so stick with us if you want to know more about the Khazalite Holds.

item.title: The Big Autumn Preview – Custodian Terminators step from the vaults
item.description: New models, new Codex, new Combat Patrol on the way for the Ten Thousand.
item.content:encoded:
Dire times have drawn the vaunted Adeptus Custodes into the fight, and now their elite Aquilon Terminators deploy alongside the next new Codex for Warhammer 40,000.

The warriors chosen to wear advanced suits of Aquilon Terminator armour are the true cream of the crop, who enter battle clad in some of the rarest and most durable plate the Imperium has ever seen. These ancient relics are usually outfitted for combat with one of two loadouts – either with lastrum storm bolters and swift Solarite power talons, or adrathic combi-destructors and devastating Solarite power gauntlets.

Like Allarus Terminators, these veteran warriors are immensely durable and can wipe out units many times their size. Their miniatures are accordingly covered in fine ornamental details, making each Terminator a display-worthy piece that together look awesome arrayed together on the battlefield.

The new Aquilon Terminators can be used in both the Age of Darkness and the 41st Millennium. Their Warhammer: The Horus Heresy rules can be found in the Liber Custodes: The Forces of the Emperor Army Book while their Warhammer 40,000 rules will be in the new Codex: Adeptus Custodes. This book follows the pattern of the previous Orks and Space Marines Codexes, with the standard softback release packing tons of background lore, hobby guides, and army rules together in a decorative slipcase.

This Codex also marks an epochal change for the Adeptus Custodes as a faction, as their datasheets are fundamentally rescaled to reflect the near-mythical demigod heroes we know and love from the lore. Even the most ‘basic’ Custodian fights at a power level beyond most Space Marine heroes, with points levels and squad sizes adjusted to make them the true most elite army in the game.*

The new Codex will be accompanied by a Combat Patrol – the perfect place to enter this new era of Imperial domination, packed with powerful warriors and advanced technology.

A Shield Captain leads a potent strike force of six Sentinel Guard and three Venatari, backed up by a towering Contemptor-Achillus Dreadnought. If you’re not worried about using this box in games of Combat Patrol, you can also build the three squads in alternate configurations, making this one of the most flexible boxes around.

Like other new Codexes in the 11th edition, you’ll also be able to pick up a faction Command Pack containing reference cards and useful tokens – invaluable for keeping your attention on the game while bolt rounds and blades fly.

This new Codex coincides with a range of newer Custodian kits getting their standalone releases, which can all be used in both Warhammer 40,000 AND Warhammer: The Horus Heresy.

The following kits are getting swanky new packaging bearing the logos for both game systems:

  • Shield Captain

  • Custodian Guard Sodality

  • Sentinel Guard Sodality

  • Venatari Sodality

  • Custodian Dreadnought

  • Telemon Heavy Dreadnought

  • Gyrfalcon Jetbike Sodality

  • Pallas Grav-attack 

  • Caladius Grav-tank

  • Caladius Annihilator Grav-tank

  • Coronus Grav-carrier

From a Warhammer 40,000 perspective, this is one of the largest expansions of the Adeptus Custodes range since the faction first launched, and gives budding Captain-Generals a vast well of reinforcements to draw from. We hope you’ve stocked up on Retributor Armour paint.

We’ll have more from the new Codex, including further details about their enhanced statlines, as we get closer to release. In the meantime, head back to the reveals hub to see what else we’ve shown off today.

item.title: The Big Autumn Preview – New Seraphon sighted
item.description: Get your first look at the new Warhammer Age of Sigmar miniature.
item.content:encoded:
A new Seraphon battletome is on the way, and with it an awesome new miniature.

Blessed Tetaxi, known as the Prophet of Tepok, is a skink with prophetic gifts. Riding atop the majestic flying titan Ma’toq, he seeks to prevent a great catastrophe.

Tetaxi has had his mind blasted by a series of cosmic secrets and terrible visions, the most foreboding of which insisted that a Great Fall was approaching that would alter the nature of reality forever. He’s represented by a jaw-dropping miniature – Tetaxi wears a headdress similar to a Starseer, while his huge flying reptile is reminiscent of the smaller Terradons. In his hand he carries the Stone of Tehemundi – said to be given to him by Tepok* – which he can use to project his visions into the minds of others.

We especially like the gap in the back of the chair so that the Skink’s tail can pass through – if you’re going to save the Mortal Realms from apocalypse, you might as well be comfortable while doing it.

As predicted by the Old Ones, Tetaxi will be accompanied by a new Seraphon battletome. It’s packed with lore and background on the merciless reptilian beings, inspirational artwork, and a miniatures showcase.

There are also new battle traits that see your army trying to Interpret the Great Plan, and be rewarded for doing so, and a pair of new Armies of Renown – including one built around Blessed Tetaxi.

Alongside the battletome comes a new Spearhead and Regiment of Renown. The Spearhead – Claws of Tepok – is based around a multitude of Skinks who are ready to aid Tetaxi in his plans. The boxed set includes a Skink Starseer, 12 Skinks, 3 Terradon Riders, and 3 Ripperdactyl Riders. If you’re looking for a fast-moving Spearhead force that makes plentiful use of Reinforcements, you’re in the right place.

The Horns of Quetzl Regiment of Renown is a great way to add a Stegadon Chief and a Stegadon to your Order- or Destruction-aligned army. Or maybe your Seraphon force needs a pair of scaled behemoths with which to launch an unstoppable stampede.

Skeleton Warriors

Animated by Liche Priests, the Skeleton Warriors form the backbone* of Tomb Kings of Khemri armies. Their serried ranks have turned the tide of many a battle. The new kit includes interchangeable shields, a full command section, and each warrior can be armed with either a spear or khopesh-style sword.

Skeleton Archers

Highly disciplined archers rain down death from afar upon the enemies of Nehekhara. You’ll be able to make them your own with interchangeable heads and quivers, and options for decorations, including arrows stuck in the ground and scuttling scarabs.

Skeleton Chariots

item.title: The Big Autumn Preview – Roleplay in the underhive
item.description: New Necromunda game revealed!
item.content:encoded:
Warhammer Necromunda Roleplay offers completely different ways to explore the underhive, and you’ll soon learn that it’s a large and dangerous place with much more to see and be killed by than just gang battles.

Been wondering why the new Necromunda Core Set proudly displays the word “Skirmish” on the front of the box? Well, it’s to distinguish it from the new Necromunda Roleplay. As the name suggests, it’s a fully-fledged, miniatures-driven RPG, allowing you to participate in immersive stories that will take you from the underhive to the ash wastes. 

You play as a group of bounty-hunting Venators taking on jobs set by the Arbitrator, the equivalent of a games master, who presents the story to the other players, adjudicating on the rules of the game, and unfolding the narrative created by the actions of the players. It’s compatible with the full range of Necromunda miniatures, and comes with some fantastic and characterful new models, starting with those representing your team – these four Iconic Characters.

These player characters are an Escher Assassin, Orlock Gunslinger, Squat Fixer, and Goliath Champion. They each have rules in the box to get you started quickly, and they all have alternate builds if you want to craft your own Venators.

You’ll encounter a variety of interesting personalities in your journeys, and some of those in the two included adventures can be nicely represented by the five Adversary miniatures in the box – a Scabber, a Saboteur, a Hive Preacher, a Cadaver Merchant, and a Heretek with a servo-skull.*

Of course, no expedition through the underhive or ash wastes is complete without gunning down some goons – step forward Hive Scum. These eight no-name mooks can be built with a wide variety of weapon options and give you plenty of opportunity to test your skills in marksmanship and swordplay as you hunt down targets and investigate mysterious goings-on.

Along with the 18 brand-new plastic miniatures, the Core Set includes the 224-page Core Rulebook, which includes plenty of lore, along with rules for playing the game, creating your own characters and how they advance and improve their skills between adventures. There are also tips for the Arbitrator and two complete adventures – ‘An Abominable Intelligence’ where you hunt down a Van Saar Heretek, and ‘The Pilgrimage of Bones’, which sees you tasked with taking out a Cawdor preacher on behalf of the Corpse Harvesters Guild.

At some point in your adventures, you’re going to get into a fight, and the box includes two double-sided card playmats depicting regions of the underhive and ash wastes where your Venators will face their foes, and 11 player handouts for quick rules reference for the miniatures in the box. There’s also an Arbitrator’s screen packed with useful reference information for the Arbitrator, and allowing them to hide their devious plans from the players.

Combat encounters play out with a system that will be recognisable to Necromunda Skirmish players, utilising miniatures who have Single and Double actions, rolls to hit and injuries – all with a roleplay twist. You’ll also notice a D10 and D100 in the box, alongside the familiar D6, Firepower and Injury dice, which work with your characters’ skills to show you what you need to roll.

In essence, whenever you want to do something, whether it’s trying to fill a Hive Scum with las-rounds or intimidate a source into giving up information, you need to roll below a target score based on your skill value and a difficulty modifier. Let’s take a look at a character sheet to see some of these.

Ophelia Skar here has a WS of 61 and BS of 49, so she’s more proficient with her stiletto sword than her laspistol. She has a variety of skills, including Acrobatics, Intimidate and Stealth, which will inform how you play her in your adventures. The other Iconic Characters have different mixes of skills and abilities, so working together is key to overcoming foes and whatever cunning obstacles your Arbitrator lays for you.

If you want to make your own characters, there are 50 blank character sheets in the box, and the Core Rulebook contains full rules for creating Venators hailing from the six Clan Houses, each with their own backgrounds, archetypes, and skill sets. There is also a seventh origin, the Underhiver, with their own selection of backgrounds and archetypes, as well as the option to play a Squat. 

Necromunda Roleplay will launch alongside the first in a series of expansions – Journal Apocrypha: Denizens of the Hive – Adversaries Book 1. This 48-page journal includes profiles for 51 additional potential Adversaries – or allies – using the wide variety of Necromunda miniatures.** 

These range from members of the six Clan Houses to Enforcers, Ogryns, hive dwellers, exotic beasts, and even the infamous Kal Jericho and Scabs, who’ve been known to recruit Venators to aid them on their own adventures. If your Arbitrator is feeling particularly mean, you might even end up facing off against a mighty Ambot…

Both the Warhammer Necromunda Roleplay Core Set and the first journal will be available soon, and we’ll delve deeper into the game and how it works before release. In the meantime, head back to the Big Autumn Preview Hub to see what else we’ve revealed.

Four new heroes get ready to take on Gelgus Pust and his plague-infested followers with Agents of the Order Azyr – the first expansion for Warhammer Quest: Darkwater.

But who are these heroic adventurers willing to risk their lives to cleanse the Jade Abbey and remove the corruption of Nurgle? Safiya Ashcross is a witch hunter who has earned a reputation for ruthlessness. In battle she can buff her fellow heroes or debuff enemies. 

Caul Durnan is a sharpshooter who has travelled with Ashcross for years. The former Wildercorps marksman is equipped with customised bolts, each designed to be used against different targets. 

Brother Belias is a battle-priest, whose faith in the Great Wheel alters his Defence and Hit characteristics. 

Finally, Ignus Sharn is a Bright Wizard who has been all but expelled from the Collegiate Arcane. Assigned to Ashcross’s ragtag retinue of killers, thieves, and outcasts, the spellcaster’s volatile nature can inflict damage on both his enemies and himself, if he’s not careful.*

If you’ve already played through the campaign in Warhammer Quest: Darkwater, these new heroes offer up a fresh challenge for another playthrough. If you’re still struggling to reclaim the Jade Abbey, Ashcross and her ragtag band bring a fresh range of skills to help you overcome the Maggotkin of Nurgle. For example, just take a look at what Caul’s customised bolts can do:

Customised Bolts

Pick 1 of the following effects to apply the next time this hero attacks using the attack profile above:

Armour-piercing Bolts: Subtract 1 from the target’s Defence characteristic for that attack.

Cluster Bolts: After making the attack roll, roll a dice for each enemy next to the target. On a 3+, inflict 1 damage on that enemy.

Swerving Bolts: The target of that attack does not have to be visible. 

New heroes also means new equipment and rewards. Sticking with Durnan, the marksman can be equipped with a shadow-cursed bolt that can be fired through a line of enemies. Such sharpshooting deserves a reward, and the wayfarer’s greatcoat is not only stylish, but can help protect Durnan (or any hero that wears it) from incoming attacks.

item.title: The Big Autumn Preview – Night Goblins hit the gridiron
item.description: A new team bounces onto the Blood Bowl pitch.
item.content:encoded:
From deep underground come the Night Goblins team for Blood Bowl, and they’ve brought Squigs with them. Lots of Squigs!

Night Goblins are known for cackling maniacally, being obsessed with mushrooms, and using moon iconography. You could say they’re a few toadstools short of a cluster, but when it comes to Blood Bowl that can be a blessing.

While their overground cousins rely on secret weapons, and other underground teams use technology or fleshcraft to win games, the Night Goblins have their vicious, bouncy friends, introducing four new positionals – Cave Squigs, Squig Wranglers, Squig Hoppers, and Squig Herders. The kit includes two of each of these, along with six Night Goblin Linemen.

Goblin Linemen might not run rampant on the pitch but they are annoying little critters who are difficult to get hold of with Dodge and Stunty, and also difficult to get away from with Taunt and Shadowing. Cave Squigs and Squig Hoppers both have Pogo, making them pretty mobile, but you’ll need to keep your Squig Herders nearby so they don’t succumb to the ominously-named Squig Rage. Finally, the Squig Wranglers are ST7 Ball & Chain players – what could possibly go wrong?

The Night Goblins are a fun, characterful team that bring a lot of new options to the Blood Bowl pitch. As with any Stunty team, they’ll need a skilful (and lucky) coach to get the best out of them, but if you can control the chaos, you’ll be onto a winner.

Rules for unleashing all this Squiggy goodness can be found in the forthcoming 23rd issue of Spike! Journal.

It’s also packed with background on Night Goblin teams, including the legendary Eight Peaks Loonatics, rules for the spiteful shroom and bat Squig balls that come with the team kit, a coaches’ guide to get the best from your gobbos, and all your favourite regular columns such as Ask Lord Borak and Coffin Corner.

item.title: Miniatures Showcase – Cargo-8 Conversions
item.description: Get ready to head out on the Ash Road with these incredible Ridgehaulers.
item.content:encoded:
We’re a few weeks into the new edition of Necromunda and our friends in the Warhammer Design Studio have been hard at work converting some suitable vehicles for their gangs.

Lucy

For my Cargo-8 Ridgehauler I really wanted the whole piece to feel ramshackle and upcycled. This crew roam the ash wastes looking for the next prize to chop up and sell to the highest bidder. Times are tough in the underhive though, and the crew have had to modify their vehicle on the fly using scraps and spares meant for sale just to keep this rig rolling!

You’ll see they’re transporting the remains of an Arvus Lighter and the front of the rig features the drilldozer from the front of a Goliath Rockgrinder.

Graham

After reading Spire of Primus, I was inspired by a piece of art which had an Enforcer patrol with two Ironcrawlers with cages on their back. I took this idea and developed it into what an armoured version for transporting VIPs (very important prisoners) would look like. I modified the Munitorum Armoured Container to look more like the back of a contemporary police van by adding barred windows and seating for those who have been deemed unworthy in the eyes of the Pax Helmawr. The main cab was slightly altered to fit the armour of the Enforcers and their trusty Cyber-mastiff (who takes pride of place by sticking their head out of the window).

The whole vehicle was then painted in the same colour scheme of my Enforcers while making the container slightly darker to give the feeling of a much older piece of equipment which has been in service for many years. The last job was to add a smattering of dirt and ash to the lower half of the vehicle, where dirt would naturally develop and build up after a long drive through the ash wastes.

Paul

The Cargo-8 Ridgehauler is such a great kit that I didn't really feel the need to convert it, I simply wanted to paint lots of them! Luckily the kit allows you to add up to four trailers. I had one goal I wanted to achieve – to make the Ridgehaulers appear a little heavier and sit deeper into the ground. Tyres on large heavy vehicles bulge and flatten out where they contact the ground, so my goal would prove to be an epic task as it involved sanding flat the tread of 32 wheels and making sure every wheel was the same height.

Dean

When the Cargo-8 challenge was suggested, I pulled one of those nagging projects from the back of my mind – Guild of Coin leased heavy industry vehicles. When I’d said the idea out loud, I had to follow through with it! Luckily, the old Galvanic Servohaulers had been made available on a Made To Order, so I grabbed a set and started work.

The truck cabs were enclosed with plasticard and wire mesh to give the models a heavier look. This enabled me to save the crew to use in the future to make the workers and guards to go along with the vehicles. The vehicles were sprayed with Leadbelcher, and then a rough red/brown layer was applied to the panel areas, followed by yellow applied via stippling to create a worn, and chipped look, emphasised by some added silver sponge chipping. An Agrax Earthshade wash was then applied to tint and unify the whole model, followed by more washes applied in streaks to emphasise that worn look.

These were intended to be used as terrain pieces on ash waste setups, but there is a very good chance I’m going to be making more, along with the workers and guards I mentioned. Now the new edition of Necromunda is here, maybe it’s time to make a new gang – perhaps a Guild of Coin-sponsored Outcast gang…

Thanks, folks! All of Ridgehaulers look ripe for a heist – we recommend some Orlock Outrider Quads to launch a speedy raid and quickly escape with your stolen swag.

Over the past few days we’ve been looking at updated rules for various Space Marine factions from the Blood Angels to the Black Templars that will be available once the upcoming Codex: Space Marines launches. Today, we’re finishing off with some of the more Codex-compliant Chapters who also get their own detachments.

Salamanders

The Salamanders have a very particular love of close-range firepower, and that returns in the renovated Forgefather’s Seekers detachment. Now that the Devastator doctrine from the new Combat Doctrines army rule lets you give your guns Assault anyway, this detachment lets you use that doctrine an additional time per game, while improving Vulkan He’stan’s effect on Infernus Squads by letting them perform actions after advancing or falling back. 

DETACHMENT RULES

VULKAN’S QUEST

Tireless in his pursuit of the Primarch’s legacy, Forgefather Vulkan He’stan annihilates any who impede his quest. Favouring swift, aggressive assaults, he and his warriors close rapidly with the enemy, destroying them at close range with ruthless efficiency.

  • You can select the devastator doctrine one additional time per battle.

  • Friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES units’ ranged attacks that target a unit within 12”, have +1 S.

If your army includes a VULKAN HE’STAN unit, friendly INFERNUS SQUAD units have the following:

  • When this unit is selected to make an advance/fall-back move, that advance/fall-back move does not prevent this unit from being eligible to start an action.

  • When this unit starts an action, that action does not prevent this unit from being eligible to shoot.

Restrictions: Your army can include SALAMANDERS units, but it cannot include any ADEPTUS ASTARTES units drawn from any other Chapter.

Changes to the way that common Torrent weapons like flamers work – now having a fixed number of shots with the Blast ability – means they can’t be fired while engaged even when fighting Vehicles and Monsters… unless you’re the Salamanders, who have spent the last 10,000 years shooting flamers at things and have gotten rather good at it. 

The Forged in Fire stratagem strips away all the downsides so you can cook your foes at point-blank range, and if you’d rather fall back before shooting instead, Wrath and Ruin activates an alternative doctrine for extra flexibility.

FORGED IN FIRE (1CP)

FORGEFATHER’S SEEKERS STRATAGEM

The Salamanders are masters of the flamer, wielding such weapons with supreme precision and utilising them even in the press of melee combat.

WHEN: Your Shooting phase, when a friendly engaged ADEPTUS ASTARTES unit is selected to shoot.

TARGET: That ADEPTUS ASTARTES unit. 

EFFECT: Your unit’s [TORRENT] weapons:

  • Do not have [BLAST].

  • Have [CLOSE-QUARTERS].

  • Have +1 A.

WRATH AND RUIN (1CP)

FORGEFATHER’S SEEKERS STRATAGEM

Having drawn their enemies in, Space Marine battle-brothers fall back and open fire at point-blank range before thundering forward to put any survivors to death.

WHEN: Your Command phase.

TARGET: One ADEPTUS ASTARTES infantry unit. 

EFFECT: The assault doctrine or tactical doctrine is active for your unit, until the start of your next Command phase.

Raven Guard

Now that Phobos-armoured units get a speed boost in return for lighter armour, the Raven Guard are masters of the movement game – and the Shadowmark Talon enhances their stealth so they can rush towards objectives with impunity. Where before they only got the Benefit of Cover while 12” away at least, now every ADEPTUS ASTARTES unit in your army has Stealth by default. 

DETACHMENT RULES

SHADOW TACTICS

The Raven Guard are renowned for their uncanny ability to move unseen, cloaking themselves in darkness as they close in upon their prey. Aethon Shaan is a true master at harnessing these abilities, withdrawing and redeploying his battle-brothers to draw the enemy out of formation.

Friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES units have Stealth. Friendly PHOBOS/SCOUT SQUAD units have -3" detection range.

Friendly AETHON SHAAN units have the following ability:

Unparalleled Tactician: (Once per battle round, per army) When you use the Into Darkness stratagem, that use is -1CP.

On top of that, PHOBOS and SCOUT units get -3” to their detection range, while Chapter Master all-star Aethon Shaan can still zoop up into Strategic Reserves for free once per battle round. 

The new Suppressed Weapons stratagem is a great way to take advantage of your hidden troops, as one INFANTRY unit can open up with their full firepower and yet remain safely hidden from return fire. They don’t even need to be part of the Phobos gang, so throw it on Eradicators with Heavy Bolters if you really want to and hose a big swarm from across the map.

SUPPRESSED WEAPONS (1CP)

SHADOWMARK TALON STRATAGEM

The Raven Guard commonly utilise integral suppressors, flash-hiders and other technology to dampen weapon reports and conceal muzzle flare, enabling battle-brothers to fire on unsuspecting foes without giving away their positions.

WHEN: Your Shooting phase, when a friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES INFANTRY unit has shot.

TARGET: That ADEPTUS ASTARTES INFANTRY unit. 

EFFECT: Those attacks do not prevent your unit from being hidden.

In addition to these two, the Ultramarines, Iron Hands, Imperial Fists and White Scars will also be getting updates to their special detachments.* Each features four enhancements and six stratagems, so you’ll have a mighty toolbox at your fingertips, and the detachments for the Iron Hands, Imperial Fists and White Scars are 2DP, opening up all sorts of options when you combine them with one of the many 1DP detachments from the Codex.

What ideas will you come up with? Shadowmark Talon and Phobos Shadow Force make your vanguard troops extra sneaky and hard to draw a bead on, while the Imperial Fists’ Ceramite Sentinels detachment is practically tailor-made to pair with Gravis Siege Force to create a legendary defensive line.

See the full spread of extra detachments in the Warhammer 40,000 app when Codex: Space Marines releases. It’s up for pre-order on Saturday, so it won’t be long now!

* An earlier version of this article said that White Scars weren't getting their own detachment. In a lightning manoeuvre typical of the sons of the Khan, one has just dropped into our inbox. White Scars players will be getting the Spearpoint Task Force for 2 DP.

item.title: Space Marines Detachments – Space Wolves, Black Templars, and Deathwatch
item.description: Updated detachments for non-compliant Chapters are coming.
item.content:encoded:
Following on from yesterday’s look at updated Blood Angels and Dark Angels rules, today’s preview has three more Chapters under the spotlight – the Space Wolves, Black Templars, and Deathwatch. Let’s see what they’ll be doing when the upcoming Codex: Space Marines comes out.

Space Wolves

There’s a lot to get through today, so we’re going to make like Phobos-armoured marines and move 33% faster than before. Space Wolves get most of the same boosts as general Space Marine units, such as the extra point of Toughness on many datasheets – including Bjorn the Fell-handed – and have some unit abilities tweaked to work better with the new Space Marine paradigm.

Grey Hunters, for instance, have re-learned how to work in 5-man teams.

you can split this unit into two units, each containing as equal a number of models as possible (when splitting a unit in this way, make a note of which models form each of the two new units).

Grey Hunters must be taken in a squad of 10 as before, but now you can split them up into two 5-man units before deployment. This can help you cover much more ground and will give Space Wolves armies an edge in action-heavy missions.

Detachment-wise, the Space Wolves see Saga of the Beastslayer and Saga of the Great Wolf come back with minor tweaks – at 1DP and 2DP respectively – while the Champions of Fenris detachment takes a far more aggressive stance and replaces all three of its Stratagems with new, more deadly options.

CHAMPION’S GUIDANCE (1CP)

CHAMPIONS OF FENRIS STRATAGEM

A paragon of Fenrisian savagery, this champion guides his warriors with confidence and precision. 

WHEN: Fight phase, when a friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES CHARACTER unit is selected to fight.

TARGET: That ADEPTUS ASTARTES CHARACTER unit. 

EFFECT: Your unit’s melee attacks can re-roll hit rolls of 1 and wound rolls of 1.

HEROIC RESOLVE (2CP)

CHAMPIONS OF FENRIS STRATAGEM

This warrior’s indomitable fortitude is the stuff of legend, galvanizing his pack to remain standing before an avalanche of incoming attacks.

WHEN: Your opponent’s Shooting phase or the Fight phase, when an enemy unit targets a friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES CHARACTER unit.

TARGET: That ADEPTUS ASTARTES CHARACTER unit. 

EFFECT: Attacks that target your unit have -1 D until that enemy unit has attacked.

Otherwise, the units you know and love are still fighting fit after these changes, and you can combine the detachments here with any from the Space Marines Codex. 

Black Templars

The Black Templars have much more of a mix-up with their rules, as the three detachments they get in this update – Fist of the God-Emperor, Vow-sworn Crusaders, and Marshal’s Household – are all either changed or new. While the army previously had their own army rule in place of Oath of Moment, now they adhere to the new Combat Doctrines rule while the swearing of Templar Vows has been moved to the Vow-sworn Crusaders detachment.

DETACHMENT RULES

TEMPLAR VOWS

On the eve of battle, the Black Templars gather to be led in prayer and contemplation by their champions. United in their hatred of the foe, they swear a mighty vow to uphold in the battle ahead.

At the start of the first battle round, you can select one Vow listed below. That Vow is active for friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES units until the end of the battle.

ABHOR THE WITCH, DESTROY THE WITCH

This unit’s melee attacks that target a PSYKER unit:

  • Have [PRECISION].

  • Have [LANCE]. 

ACCEPT ANY CHALLENGE, NO MATTER THE ODDS

Friendly melee attacks that target a unit with a T greater than this unit’s S have +1 to wound rolls.

UPHOLD THE HONOUR OF THE EMPEROR

Friendly INFANTRY units have:

  • At the end of your Movement phase, if this unit is controlling an objective, that objective is secured.

  • When this unit is selected to make an advance move, that advance move does not prevent this unit from being eligible to start an action.

Restrictions: Your army can include BLACK TEMPLARS units, but it cannot include any ADEPTUS ASTARTES units drawn from any other Chapter.

As it costs only 2DP, Vow-sworn Crusaders fits nicely with plenty of the 1DP detachments kicking around in the new Codex, so if you want to Accept Any Challenge, No Matter the Odds and double down on close combat carnage with the Assault Brethren, you can.

Getting access to the Assault Doctrine’s ability to advance and charge is great news for the Emperor’s Champion, whose slimmed-down Sigismund’s Heir ability now gives a lovely +1 to charge rolls and doesn’t require them to end up engaged with a Character. Black Templars fans may lament the loss of the ability to give him Devastating Wounds once per battle, but don’t worry – it’s just baked right into the Black Sword’s Strike profile now.

The new Fist of the God-Emperor detachment, meanwhile, takes the part of the old Vindication Task Force ability that lets Crusader Squads make surge moves towards objectives and pairs it with stratagems and enhancements that directly boost the Black Templars’ iconic infantry squad. Giving big squads the Righteous Fervour upgrade will make them excellent objective-holders as they power towards the centre of the battlefield, safe in the knowledge that a few dead Neophytes only makes them get to their target quicker.

ENHANCEMENTS

RIGHTEOUS FERVOUR [UPGRADE]

With their zealous hatred stoked red-hot by furious sermons and inflammatory prayers, Companions of Vehemence are filled with a wrathful vigour. Only the deaths of the God-Emperor’s enemies can assuage their fury, and they will let nothing delay them from unleashing it.

CRUSADER SQUAD unit only. This unit can re-roll Advance rolls.

Deathwatch

Finally, the Deathwatch get an update to their classic 3DP Black Spear Task Force detachment that ties their Mission Tactics to Combat Doctrines and gently upgrades a few of their stratagems, but the real party piece is the new 1DP Deathwatch Support detachment that uses the same detachment rule as the Black Spear Task Force, but allows a 500 point force of Deathwatch to be taken in any Space Marines army.

DETACHMENT RULES

MISSION TACTICS

Thousands of years of collated strategic data and hard-won combat experience have provided the Deathwatch with the ultimate battlefield tactics to combat almost any foe.

FUROR TACTICS 

When the enemy horde grows close, the Deathwatch will be tasked with the decimation of their core. Aiming not for clinical kills but for maximum destruction over a wide area, they tear the heart from the enemy army.

MALLEUS TACTICS 

When the giants of war lumber forth, the Deathwatch will adopt Malleus tactics. Even the largest behemoth has a weak point, and the archives of the Deathwatch number them all.

PURGATUS TACTICS 

By adopting Purgatus tactics, the Deathwatch focus their deadly ire upon the commanders of the enemy host, assassinating them one after another with pitiless head shots and killing thrusts of the blade.

Friendly KILL TEAM units with this ability have the following abilities:

Furor Tactics: If the devastator doctrine is active for your unit, your unit’s attacks have [SUSTAINED HITS 1].

Malleus Tactics: If the tactical doctrine is active for your unit, your unit’s attacks have [LETHAL HITS]. 

Purgatus Tactics: If the assault doctrine is active for your unit, your unit’s attacks that target an enemy unit within 9" of this unit have [PRECISION].

If you’ve ever wanted a team of elite veterans to hunt xenos prey while the rest of your army fights on the front line, this is the best way to do it. You can even give your best squad the ability to Deep Strike with the classic Beacon Angelis enhancement – provided they have a Character leading them – so if all you want is a single scary Kill Team ruining your opponent’s back line, you can do it.

All of these new rules will go live on the Warhammer 40,000 app when Codex: Space Marines releases, and with pre-orders happening this very weekend, you won’t have long to wait.

item.title: Space Marines detachments – Blood Angels and Dark Angels
item.description: Updated detachments for non-compliant Chapters are on the way.
item.content:encoded:
The upcoming release of Codex: Space Marines heralds significant changes for almost every part of the faction, from datasheets to detachments. This also has a knock-on effect on other Space Marine factions that rely on those core rules, so over the next couple of days, we’re going to see how less Codex-compliant Chapters are being updated – starting with the Blood Angels and Dark Angels.

Blood Angels

When Codex: Space Marines releases, the Blood Angels, Dark Angels, Space Wolves, Black Templars, and Deathwatch will all get an overhaul of their units and detachments in the Warhammer 40,000 app, while the more Codex-compliant Chapters like the Salamanders and Imperial Fists will get updates to their specialist detachments. 

The Blood Angels, for instance, get a new 2DP version of Angelic Inheritors that focuses their detachment rule on the ability to re-roll 1s for Hit and Wound rolls (that everybody chose anyway) while still offering four enhancements and six stratagems with plenty of familiar favourites. Their new Measured Strategist stratagem is a versatile tool that lets a unit slip into whichever Combat Doctrine they please, so even if most of your army fancies having Assault on their guns, Dante and his Sanguinary Guard can advance and charge right into the thick of it.

MEASURED STRATEGIST (1CP)

ANGELIC INHERITORS STRATAGEM

Stern and level-headed, this Blood Angels commander is a beacon of composure amidst the tempest of his brothers’ fury, providing much-needed tactical guidance for his impetuous battle-brothers. 

WHEN: Your Command phase.

TARGET: One friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES CHARACTER unit. 

EFFECT: Select one combat doctrine. That combat doctrine is active for your unit until the start of your next Command phase.

As true sons of Sanguinius will know, Angelic Inheritors specifically affects CHARACTER units – whether they’re running around on their own or leading their subordinates – and they’re getting a few upgrades of their own. Commander Dante now activates the Assault and Tactical doctrines for his unit at all times, while everyone’s favourite Black Rage survivor Mephiston is stronger, tougher, and faster than ever.

Dark Angels

Over on the Dark Angels side of the aisle, their Wrath of the Rock detachment also returns at 2DP, primed for being combined with the wide assortment of 1DP detachments in Codex: Space Marines. 

Most of their enhancements and stratagems are the classics you know and love, but Armour of Contempt and Leonine Aggression* get swapped out for In Sacrifice, Victory and Knights of Iron. The former lets a Deathwing or Ravenwing unit secure an objective with their dying breath, while the latter sends skilled Ravenwing pilots and riders buzzing around seemingly solid terrain with the MOBILE keyword.

Atop their snarling mechanical steeds, the warriors of the Ravenwing surge through seemingly impassable terrain, smashing through rubble and ruin to unleash the wrath of the Unforgiven upon unsuspecting targets. 

WHEN: Your Movement/Charge phase, when a friendly RAVENWING unit is selected to move or declares a charge.

TARGET: That RAVENWING unit. 

EFFECT: Your unit has MOBILE.

We’ve already seen Roboute Guilliman’s new datasheet, so how does his brother Primarch stack up against the Avenging Son? Lion El’Jonson gets the same Toughness 10, 16 Wounds upgrade as Guilliman, but also adds some new abilities to his belt. 

The Watchers gives him a permanent Feel No Pain 4+ against all psychic attacks and mortal wounds even when he hasn’t picked his No Hiding From the Watchers aura – which now confers Feel No Pain 5+ against psychic attacks and mortal wounds to units within 6”.

Meanwhile, his Master Strategist lets him pick a Combat Doctrine to have active every turn, in addition to the one you normally pick. And for those that are worried, the Lion keeps his Dark Angels Bodyguard, Emperor's Shield and his Primarch of the First Legion abilities.

The Inner Circle Task Force and Darkflight Pursuit detachments also stick around at 1DP each, and the latter now gives Outrider Squads the BATTLELINE keyword for some proper high speed Ravenwing action. If you’re a particular fan of Deathwing Knights, try combining Wrath of the Rock with the new Terminator Storm Force detachment for some terrifying Terminator-based synergies.

Tomorrow, we’ll be showing off changes for the Space Wolves, Black Templars, and Deathwatch – including a 1DP detachment that lets you add some Deathwatch troops to other Space Marines armies. We’ll have the more Codex-compliant reveals the day after. See you there!

item.title: AoS Coach on the new Sons of Behemat
item.description: Get some army building ideas from a top Warhammer Age of Sigmar player.
item.content:encoded:
The ground is shaking, the boulders are flying, and the Sons of Behemat are lumbering towards their next big scrap. Today, Anthony Magro from AoS Coach reveals the new battletome builds that could bring the biggest smash to the battlefield. 

Anthony:  The last time I wrote about the Sons of Behemat for Warhammer Community was back in 2021, when the army’s game plan was reasonably straightforward – put an enormous Mega-Gargant on an objective and ask your opponent what they planned to do about it. 

They may still prefer to settle arguments by throwing their weight around, but the new Battletome: Sons of Behemat gives them many more options than simply marching forwards and hoping something breaks.

The Sons’ defining strengths remain: gargants are enormous, hard-hitting monsters with devastating charges and enough battlefield presence to demand an immediate response. But the new battletome gives them more tools, from Ma Maegran, Boss-stompers, and Rock-hurlers to specialised units that seize objectives, bombard the enemy, screen vulnerable areas, and create openings for a gargant to strike. They still solve problems with brute force, but now they have more say in which problem gets flattened first. That opens the door to combat-focused forces, ranged armies, specialised-unit builds, and devastating all-out assaults led by Kragnos. 

Here are three mighty gatherings of gargants that could leave an unforgettable mark on the Mortal Realms. 

Sons of Behemat – 1970/2000 pts 
Battle Formation: Looting Leviathans 
Spell Lore: Lore of Behemat 
Prayer Lore: Lore of the World Titan 
Manifestation Lore: Primal Energy
Battle Tactics: Burning for Vengeance, Legend of the Parch 

General’s Regiment 
King Brodd (430) 
• General
Kraken-eater Mega-Gargant (370)
• Artefacts of Power: Krakenskin Sandals (10) 

Regiment 1
Beast-smasher Mega-Gargant (380)
• Heroic Trait:  Unreasonable Tyrant (0)
• Realm-Shaking Rampage: Earthshaking Roar (20)
Warstomper Mega-Gargant (390)
Boss-stompers (370) 

The Boss-stompers might be LITTLE by Sons of Behemat standards, but there's nothing little about what happens when three of them reach combat. This army is built around getting them there, then having the bigger gargants pile into the same fight and make an already dangerous unit considerably nastier. 

The Beast-smasher is their natural partner. Rather than simply being another Mega-Gargant sent off to smash things by itself, I want it fighting alongside the Boss-stompers. I'll often build the Beast-smasher towards STRIKE-FIRST using the army's battle traits, allowing it to swing before the Boss-stompers and use Leader of the Pack to give their melee weapons Crit (2 Hits). Earthshaking Roar can also stop the unfortunate target from using commands, which is particularly useful when you don't want All-out Defence taking some of the sting out of what's coming next. 

Looting Leviathans is my preferred battle formation for this version of the army, because once the Boss-stompers make their charge I want them getting to the thing that actually matters. Argy Bargy can add 3" to their pile-in moves for the rest of the turn, giving them a 6" pile-in, while Get to the Goods lets a charging BIG or LITTLE unit pass across enemy models in non-MONSTER units while doing so. A screen that looked perfectly sensible at the start of the Charge phase can suddenly become much less reassuring. 

LOOTING LEVIATHANS

Passive

GET TO THE GOODS

When shiny treasure or barrels of grog are sighted, these gargants wade through ranks of little 'uns without pause.

Effect: Each time a friendly BIG or LITTLE unit that charged in the same turn makes a pile-in move, that unit can pass across enemy models in non-MONSTER units.

The rest of the army helps make that engagement happen. The Warstomper can move another BIG or LITTLE unit 2D6" in the Movement phase, while the Kraken-eater and the Beast-smasher's Unreasonable Tyrant heroic trait can each add 1 to the Boss-stompers' charge roll. King Brodd can then add 1 to the Rend of their melee weapons with Power of Behemat prayer, while remaining a serious threat in his own right. 

There's even a nasty reversal if your opponent decides to charge the Boss-stompers first. Quit Hogging Da Fun! lets them bring a nearby BIG unit into the fight immediately after they attack in the enemy combat phase. On my turn, the Beast-smasher sets up the Boss-stompers. On yours, the Boss-stompers can drag one of the big lads into the punch-up with them. 

I've deliberately taken four different Mega-Gargants here to maximise their different Once Per Turn (Army) abilities, but there is another way to build the same idea. If I swapped King Brodd for Ma Maegran, I would also replace the Warstomper with a second unit of Boss-stompers. That redundancy matters because Chooser of the Mighty can sacrifice a LITTLE model to return a destroyed non-UNIQUE BIG unit, and I don't want to weaken my only Boss-Stomper unit just to bring a Mega-Gargant back. 

Either way, the plan is wonderfully straightforward – get the gang together, pick the biggest problem on the battlefield, and introduce it to an unreasonable number of clubs. 

Sons of Behemat – 1990/2000 pts 
Battle Formation: Heirs of the Old Ways 
Spell Lore: Lore of Behemat 
Prayer Lore: Brodd’s Bellows (Scourge of Aqshy) 
Manifestation Lore: Primal Energy 
Battle Tactics: Blazing Onslaught, Burning for Vengeance 

General’s Regiment 
Ma Maegran (370) 
• General 
Ancient Ghyrochs (0) 
Boss-stompers (370) 

Regiment 1 
King Brodd (430) 
Gatebreaker Mega-Gargant (400) 
• Heroic Trait:  Always First In (0) 
• Artefacts of Power: Glowy Lantern (20) 
• Realm-Shaking Rampage: Earthshaking Roar (20) 
Rock-hurlers (380) 

Sons of Behemat armies have never exactly been famous for subtle ranged warfare, but the new Rock-hurlers give you a very different way to approach the battlefield. Rather than racing everything into combat, this army wants to apply pressure from range, force the opponent to come towards you, and then let King Brodd and the Boss-stompers finish whatever survives the opening bombardment. 

The Gatebreaker is what makes that shooting package really work. Rip It Up and Chuck It lets it uproot nearby terrain and improve the Rock-hurlers' or its own shooting, giving each Rock-hurler model an extra attack with its ranged weapons. The Rock-hurlers can then adapt with Drop, Toss or Roll depending on what the turn demands with extra range when the target is keeping its distance, better accuracy when you need the damage, or Shoot in Combat when somebody inevitably decides charging the gargants will solve the problem. 

Ma Maegran fits beautifully behind that firing line. While she stays close to another Sons of Behemat Monster, The Wandering Witch makes her invisible to enemies more than 12" away, allowing her to sit behind the Gatebreaker and Rock-hurlers and concentrate on supporting the army rather than worrying about being picked off. I generally keep the Ancient Ghyrochs nearby too, using Shepherdess to increase Ma's power level and give me more magical options each turn. 

This is also where I really like bringing the Scourge of Aqshy season rules into the army. King Brodd is already a Priest, and the Glowy Lantern lets me make the Gatebreaker another one. That gives me two sources of the Rock Bottom prayer,* which grants a 6+ Ward and lets a unit ignore the effects of Battle Damaged. For an army built around several expensive gargants, keeping a wounded Mega-Gargant operating at full effectiveness while the opponent tries to weather the shooting can be enormously valuable. 

TITANIC TROPHIES

Deployment Phase

GLOWY LANTERN

Stolen from the aelves of Hysh after a botched alliance, this aetherquartz jar was at first carried around just because it was shiny. Over time, it has granted its bearer an innate power.

Effect: If this unit is a WIZARD or PRIEST, add 1 to its power level for the rest of the battle. Otherwise, pick either the WIZARD (1) or PRIEST (1) keyword. This unit has that keyword for the rest of the battle.

Heirs of the Old Ways is my preferred battle formation here. This list wants its firing lanes and support pieces operating cleanly, so being able to interfere with enemy Wizards or Priests and potentially clear away the manifestations they have summoned helps stop the army from being pinned down before it can dictate the engagement. 

Once the enemy does close the distance, that is where Brodd and the Boss-stompers take over. The shooting does not necessarily have to destroy the target outright – it just has to make the fight that follows unfair in your favour. 

You could double down and replace the Boss-stompers with another unit of Rock-hurlers, or trade them for three individual Mancrushers to gain more scoring pieces and cleaner sacrifices for Chooser of the Mighty. If you do take three Mancrushers, it is also worth considering the Hammer Throw Realm-shaking Rampage, which lets you throw a Mancrusher 3D6" and potentially launch it straight into combat. I prefer the mixed version, though. Your opponent can stay back and get rocks thrown at them, or come closer and discover that the ammunition was never the biggest threat.

Sometimes the best way to control the battlefield is to make sure your opponent never gets comfortable on it. This list is built around Kragnos doing exactly that, using his 3D6” charge support to turn the opening turns into an immediate threat while the rest of the army piles in behind him. 

King Brodd is a big part of making that happen. Through World Titan’s Stride, he can add 3" to Kragnos’ Move and let him pass across enemy models and terrain as though he had FLY. Kragnos already threatens an enormous distance thanks to those 3D6” charges, so giving him even more freedom to move around screens or awkward terrain helps make sure he reaches the fight you actually care about rather than the one your opponent wants to offer you. 

Once he gets there, the Beast-smasher and Ma Maegran start layering on the support. Leader of the Pack can give Kragnos Crit (2 Hits), while Creepy Cantrips can add 1 to hit rolls for his combat attacks. Brodd can then contribute Power of Behemat for extra Rend. I don’t need every one of those effects every turn, but having access to them means Kragnos can go from being a fast hammer to an absolutely brutal one when the right target presents itself.

Ma Maegran fills a different role here to the previous list. I’m less interested in hiding her behind a shooting castle and more interested in having her follow the main assault as a mobile magical support piece. The Ancient Ghyrochs help increase her power level, giving her the casting bandwidth to keep feeding useful buffs into the front line. 

The Scourge of Aqshy Mancrusher is the cheap utility piece that makes the list tick. It can contribute to mission play, dabble in prayers through That Boy’s Not Right, and since it has the LITTLE keyword it becomes an ideal sacrifice for Chooser of the Mighty if the Beast-smasher goes down. That means I can afford to throw the Beast-smasher into dangerous combats knowing Ma may be able to bring it back later. 

This isn’t the subtle Sons list. It’s the one that wants to seize the initiative, hit first, and make the opponent start solving problems immediately. 

If Kragnos is known as the End of Empires, this army is really just trying to make sure he gets started early. 

More Than A One-Hit Wonder 

These three lists only scratch the surface of what the new Sons of Behemat battletome can do. 

You can double down on Rock-hurlers and turn the army into a much heavier ranged threat, build around multiple Boss-stomper units for redundancy, lean harder into Mancrushers for mission play, or explore very different combinations of Mega-Gargants depending on which support abilities you value most. Ma Maegran alone opens up a whole range of list-building decisions around magic, LITTLE units and bringing destroyed Mega-Gargants back into the fight. 

That is probably what I like most about this battletome. There is no longer one obvious question of which Mega-Gargants hit hardest. Instead, I find myself asking which gargants I want working together, what role each one is filling, and how those pieces help the army control the battlefield. 

The Sons of Behemat are still enormous, still destructive, and still perfectly capable of solving problems by hitting them with something the size of a building. They just have a few more ways to decide which building to use.
